name: Los Angeles Union Passenger Terminal

location.text: 800 North Alameda Street, Los Angeles, California

dates.note: Wikipedia's infobox prints 'Built 1939' and the station opened in May 1939; the terminal was commissioned in 1933.

refs.title: NRHP reference No. 80000811; added to the National Register 13 November 1980; architect John and Donald Parkinson; built by Robert E. McKee Inc. (as the Wikipedia infobox prints it)
Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument No. 101, designated 2 August 1972 (a city designation, not a state register file)
Los Angeles Union Passenger Terminal, Tracks & Shed, 800 North Alameda Street, Los Angeles, Los Angeles County, CA; Call Number: HABS CAL,19-LOSAN,64-A-
refs.note: This item is the TRACKS AND SHED (sub-record A), not the terminal building. It is recorded as evidence that a HABS group exists under the geographic call number CAL,19-LOSAN,64; the item for the terminal itself was NOT resolved and no survey number is asserted for it. Deliberately filed as `other` rather than `loc-item` so that nothing reads it as this building's own Library item.

refs.title: National Register of Historic Places Inventory — Nomination Form, Los Angeles Union Passenger Terminal, Los Angeles County, California (NPGallery)
History - Union Station Los Angeles
refs.note: The operator's own words: 'an innovative blend of Spanish Colonial, Mission Revival and Art Deco architecture now commonly referred to as Mission Moderne', completed 1939 'for a reported $11 million'.

note: Seeded 5 Sep 2026. NO survey block: the Library item that surfaced is the terminal's tracks and shed, a different structure in the same HABS group, and building a survey record on it would have attributed a shed's description to a station. The style attribution is itself contested in the sources and both readings are carried: Wikipedia's infobox says 'Moderne, Art Deco, Mission/Spanish Revival' and the operator calls it 'Mission Moderne'.
